source: CARDI (2011), "Handbook of Integrated Techniques for Increasing Wet-Season and Dry-Season Rice Productivity" (Khmer, 50pp, funded by CAVAC/ACIAR, foreword by H.E. Chan Sarun, Minister of Agriculture, dated 26 August 2011)
text: Match variety duration and mature height to the actual water regime of the field, not just the broad ecosystem type. Using a heavy/long-duration variety on a middle-terrace field where standing water drains away early causes the crop to face drought stress right at flowering. Conversely, using a light/short-duration variety on a lower-terrace field where water stays deep for longer causes the crop to still be standing in deep water when the grain is already mature, making harvest and transporting the crop out of the field difficult. In areas prone to flash flooding or to drought, farmers should specifically choose varieties bred to tolerate that stress rather than relying on general-purpose varieties.
